clue.text: 12 piece Gaelic drum

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 12 across, a word for hunted birds and animals

parts.note: a piece of something is a part of it
drum, from Gaelic druim, is a long narrow hill or ridge, as in drumlin

explanation.surface: A Celtic percussion instrument with twelve pieces, perhaps part of a drum kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 12 leads to another clue: game in the hunting sense, so a game bird is wanted. 'Drum' is not the instrument but the Gaelic hill word.
explanation.definitionFit: This plump bird is shot for sport and eaten, a classic example of game in the hunting sense.

clue.text: Daughter gripped by Ring Cycle?

indicators.note: the daughter letter is held inside the ring word

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A girl is captivated by Wagner's Ring cycle of operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring Cycle' evokes Wagner's operas; 'Cycle?' is the verb to ride a bike, the question mark marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedal is to work a bicycle's pedals, which is what cycling involves.

clue.text: Etruscans converted religious dissenters

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient Italians who changed faith became nonconformists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' fits the religious surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Recusants were those who refused to attend Church of England services, chiefly Catholics.

clue.text: A new construction: "Dog's dinner upended in barley soup"

indicators.note: the reversed mess is placed in the shuffled barley
something in the soup is in a mess, so the letters of barley are mixed
upended means turned over, so the word is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a dog's dinner is British slang for a mess

explanation.surface: A recipe described as a dog's dinner ends up upside down in the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog's dinner' sounds like food to go with the soup, but it is slang for a mess; 'soup' makes REABLY and 'upended' makes SSEM, which goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Reassembly is putting something together again, a fresh act of construction.

clue.text: Mock serious, defunct camera move

parts.note: defunct means dead
to pan is to swing a camera horizontally

explanation.surface: A film critic ridicules a dead serious camera move.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan describes a pretended straight face, solemn in jest.

clue.text: The artist Leger's funny business

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of Leger are rearranged

parts.note: the name Leger, the possessive adding no letter
Co. is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: The painter Léger runs a comic enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' turns LEGER into ELGRE; Fernand Léger is a red herring artist.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter who worked in Spain, so he is an artist.

clue.text: Mawkish something said to set dogs off at end of day

parts.words: something said to set dogs off
parts.note: mush is the call a sled driver gives to start the dogs running

indicators.note: signals the final letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A soppy sledge driver calls the team away as evening falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something excessively sentimental and sugary in feeling.

clue.text: Mike, even shorter, needs a mineral

parts.note: mike, short for microphone, shortens further to mic

explanation.surface: A microphone, cut down even more, needs a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Mica is a silicate mineral that splits into thin shiny sheets.

clue.text: Star shaped, incorporating international feature of fluted column

indicators.note: the shuffled star takes in the international letter
shaped means formed anew, so the letters of star are rearranged

explanation.surface: A star-shaped design incorporates something global into a fluted column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaped' turns STAR into STRA, with I put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stria is one of the grooves or channels that run down a fluted column.

clue.text: A Beatles' song? Not now

definitions.meaning: the day before today, a time past rather than present

explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday was a Beatles hit, and it is also the day before today, so not now.

clue.text: Top grade beverage served after opening of day residence in the country

indicators.note: the drink and grade come after the first piece in the answer
the opening of a word is its first letter, here of day

parts.note: A is the top grade in exams
cha (char) is an informal word for tea

explanation.surface: A first-class drink is brought out at dawn at a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served after' places A and CHA after the D taken from 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian second home or villa out in the countryside.

clue.text: Glacier rocks in the way of Spanish port

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters of Glacier are rearranged

parts.note: as means in the way, as in 'do as I say'

explanation.surface: Ice and boulders block the road to a harbour in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' turns GLACIER into ALGECIR; 'Glacier rocks' looks like a noun phrase about geology.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeciras is a major seaport in southern Spain on the bay facing Gibraltar.

clue.text: Keep going, drinker, for Leonardo painting

parts.note: to last is to keep going, endure
one who sups, sipping a drink, is a supper

explanation.surface: Someone urges a drinker to keep at it in front of a Renaissance masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPER here is not the meal but one who sups.
explanation.definitionFit: Da Vinci's famous mural in Milan shows Christ's final meal with the apostles.

clue.text: Halting expulsion of Lawrence, maybe, from cell?

indicators.note: the initials of Lawrence are pushed out of the cell word

parts.note: a gamete is a reproductive cell
T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, had the initials TE

explanation.surface: A cell inmate stops someone called Lawrence from being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cell' suggests a prison, but it is the biological sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of game means lame, as in a game leg, so it can describe a halting walk.

clue.text: Pamela, sad, lost without piano, is moved by a swallow

indicators.note: without means outside, so the shuffled letters go round the piano letter
lost means astray, so the letters of Pamela and sad are rearranged

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A sad Pamela, without her piano, is moved by a little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking; 'swallow' looks like the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The lump of throat cartilage in the neck visibly rises and falls when a person gulps.

clue.text: 12 piece following swing?

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 12 across: a pastime with rules

indicators.note: the piece word comes after the swing word in the answer

parts.note: to swing from a rope is to hang
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A game piece is moved after a swing, as if on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at the gallows, which is the theme of this word-guessing game.
explanation.definitionFit: This pencil-and-paper guessing game is one of the pastimes cross-referenced to 12.

clue.text: Crooked sill, in concealed places, slopes

indicators.note: the shuffled sill goes inside the word for concealed places

parts.note: hides are concealed shelters for watching birds or game

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of sill are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bent windowsill sits in hiding places on slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed places' reads as hiding spots in general but means birdwatchers' shelters; 'Crooked' rearranges the windowsill word into ILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hillsides are the sloping sides of hills, so they are slopes.

clue.text: Getting on potty around 1: 12

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 12 across: a card pastime here

parts.note: someone getting on is old

indicators.note: the word for potty goes round the numeral piece

parts.note: potty means crazy, mad
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An elderly person on a potty refers to clue 1 and clue 12.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' looks like a cross-reference to 1 across but just gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's card game in which the player left holding the odd queen loses.

clue.text: Broadcast appropriate cause of plane's sudden descent?

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
to pocket something is to appropriate or take it

explanation.surface: A broadcast reports a fitting explanation for an aircraft plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb to take.
explanation.definitionFit: An air pocket is a downdraught or region of thin air that makes an aircraft drop suddenly.

clue.text: Ultimate drink, after which sporty type won't get another round in

definitions.text: after which sporty type won't get another round in

parts.note: ultimate means last
to lap is to drink, as a cat does

explanation.surface: The final drink is called, so nobody buys another round at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'round': at the pub a round of drinks, on the track one circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race the final circuit is the one after which a runner does no more circuits.

clue.text: Bridge 12

definitions.meaning: a floating bridge supported on boats or floats
refers to the answer at 12 across: here the card pastime also called twenty-one

explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon is a floating bridge support, and also the card game also called twenty-one.

clue.text: Sucker's perm styled and fringed by amateur

indicators.note: the amateur word goes round the outside, like a fringe

parts.note: lay means not professional, amateur

indicators.note: hair that is styled is rearranged, so the letters of perm are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's amateur perm leaves the customer looking a mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe but is the fish; 'styled' rearranges the hairdo word into MPRE for the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: This eel-like fish has a round sucking mouth for attaching to its prey.

clue.text: Coarse linen strand on butter

indicators.note: in a down clue the strand word sits on top of the butter word

parts.note: a lock is a strand of hair
a ram is a butter, an animal that butts

explanation.surface: A thread of coarse fabric is spread on butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but one that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockram is an old kind of coarse linen fabric, historically made in Brittany.

clue.text: God's rejected 12

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 12 across: here a simple card pastime

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild; with the 's this gives PANS

explanation.surface: A deity's turned down a game.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's card game where players shout when two matching cards appear.

clue.text: Man possibly following a path to wedlock?

indicators.note: the island word comes after the a in the answer

parts.note: the Isle of Man is one example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man follows a path towards marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a groom but stands for the Isle of Man; brides walk up the church aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: The bride walks up the church's central passage to be married, a playful route to wedlock.

clue.text: Slapstick turn follows rap artist's introduction

indicators.note: the turn word comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: a rap on a door is a knock

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter, here of artist's

parts.note: a bout is a turn or spell of activity

explanation.surface: A comedy act follows a rapper's introduction on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rap artist' reads as a musician but splits into rap (KNOCK) and artist (A).
explanation.definitionFit: Knockabout comedy is boisterous and physical, much the same as slapstick.

clue.text: City can, if located round old city

indicators.note: the can word is put round the old city word

parts.note: a tin is a can
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A city might preserve its tins, if placed around an ancient one.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in north-west Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: 24 Kitty's 12

definitions.meaning: a shared fund of money, as in a betting pot
refers to the answer at 12 across: here a cue sport played on a table

explanation.walkthrough: The leading '24' is the clue's own number repeated in the source and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool is a shared pot of money, and it is also a cue sport on a table with pockets.

clue.text: Mark is about to be beset by anguish

indicators.note: the anguish word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: dolour is grief, anguish
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone in torment is about to be overwhelmed by grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something can mean to stain or spoil its colour, as discolouring does.

clue.text: Rude attention-getter is 12

definitions.meaning: a person who jabs someone with a finger to catch their attention, impolitely
refers to the answer at 12 across: a card pastime played for stakes

explanation.surface: Someone who rudely prods for notice is just playing a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker can be one who pokes, and it is also the bluffing card game played for money.

clue.text: Case put under fire

definitions.meaning: a casing or hard outer covering

explanation.surface: A box is put under fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell is a casing such as a nut's, and to shell is to bombard with artillery.

clue.text: Anaesthetist figure makes accommodation for PM?

parts.note: one who numbs is a numb-er
ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: An anaesthetist's number builds lodging for the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as numb-er, one who numbs. Number Ten Downing Street is the UK Prime Minister's official home.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Prime Minister lives at 10 Downing Street, commonly called by this name.
